guide.forever.campfire_process.craft: Craft the campfire from logs and sticks.
guide.forever.campfire_process.ignite: Light it with your ignition tool. See Starting a Fire if it will not light.
guide.forever.campfire_process.inputs: You need logs and sticks to build the campfire, and raw food to cook on it.
guide.forever.campfire_process.interrupt: Food left on a campfire stays there. Breaking the campfire drops whatever was on it.
guide.forever.campfire_process.outputs: Place raw food on the campfire and collect it once cooked.
guide.forever.campfire_process.place: Place the campfire on a solid surface with open space above it.
guide.forever.campfire_process.safety: Campfires damage anyone standing in them. Keep them away from walkways and from anything flammable.
guide.forever.campfire_process.summary: A lit campfire is your first cooking station. It is slow, needs no fuel, and works from the moment it is lit.
guide.forever.campfire_process.timing: Cooking on a campfire is slower than a furnace, but it consumes no fuel, which makes it the right tool early on.
guide.forever.campfire_process.title: Cooking at a Campfire
guide.forever.early_processing.automatio: Both stations accept the usual input, fuel, and output handling, so you can automate them when you want to.
guide.forever.early_processing.campfire_: The campfire is the starting point. It cooks without fuel but handles only simple work.
guide.forever.early_processing.failure: If a station cannot be crafted, check that you have a campfire available as a component along with the required bricks or metal.
guide.forever.early_processing.first_sta: Your first upgrade is a faster food-processing station built around a campfire, using mud bricks and packed mud.
guide.forever.early_processing.second_st: The general-purpose smelting station is built from bricks and iron, again around a campfire, and handles ores and other materials.
guide.forever.early_processing.summary: You move from open fire to dedicated stations as you gather better materials.
guide.forever.early_processing.title: Early Processing Stations
guide.forever.early_processing.vanilla_p: Once built, these stations behave the way you expect. Processing recipes for cooking, smelting, and blasting all work through them.
guide.forever.early_tools.bronze_upgrade: Bronze is an upgrade applied to an existing copper tool rather than a fresh craft. The result is far more durable, so keep your copper tools rather than discarding them.
guide.forever.early_tools.condition: Every tool tracks condition and can be repaired. See Equipment Condition for how repair works.
guide.forever.early_tools.copper_capabil: Copper tools are the first meaningful step up and last noticeably longer than what came before.
guide.forever.early_tools.failure: If an upgrade recipe does not appear, check that you are supplying the existing tool as an input along with the upgrade material.
guide.forever.early_tools.first_material: Your first tools are made from the materials at hand and wear out quickly.
guide.forever.early_tools.identity: Upgrading a tool keeps it recognisably the same tool. You are improving what you own, not replacing it.
guide.forever.early_tools.summary: Early tools progress by material. Each step is a real upgrade in durability and capability.
guide.forever.early_tools.title: Early Tool Progression
guide.forever.early_tools.tool_roles: Different tools suit different work. Carrying the right tool matters more than carrying the single strongest one.
guide.forever.equipment_condition.broken: At zero condition an item becomes Broken. It is unusable until repaired, but it is never destroyed and never disappears from your inventory.
guide.forever.equipment_condition.condit: Condition falls with use. A worn item still works, but its tooltip warns you before it reaches zero.
guide.forever.equipment_condition.field_: A field repair can be done anywhere with the right material. It restores part of the item's condition, enough to keep working away from home.
guide.forever.equipment_condition.readin: Hold an item to read its condition, its status, and its active path in the tooltip.
guide.forever.equipment_condition.summar: Tools and armour track condition as they are used. Condition is shown as text on the item tooltip, not by colour alone.
guide.forever.equipment_condition.title: Equipment Condition
guide.forever.equipment_condition.worksh: A workshop repair restores an item to full condition. Repairing does not reduce the item's maximum condition, so equipment does not decay permanently over time.
guide.forever.equipment_reforging.active: An item may know several paths, but only one is active at a time. The active path is shown on the tooltip.
guide.forever.equipment_reforging.identi: A reforged item keeps its identity, including its name and history. It is the same item, not a replacement.
guide.forever.equipment_reforging.paths: There is no single best tool. A path makes an item better at one kind of work rather than better at everything.
guide.forever.equipment_reforging.preser: Reforging never erases what an item already learned. Progress on a path you switch away from is kept, so you can switch back later without starting over.
guide.forever.equipment_reforging.summar: Equipment can learn specialisation paths. A pickaxe might follow the Prospector, Excavator, or Delver path, each better at a different kind of work.
guide.forever.equipment_reforging.switch: Switching the active path requires reforging. Reforging also restores the item to full condition.
guide.forever.equipment_reforging.title: Reforging and Specialisation Paths
guide.forever.fire_starting.confirm: A lit campfire gives light and smoke. If neither appears, it is still unlit.
guide.forever.fire_starting.craft_igniti: Craft an ignition tool from flint before you need it. Without one, a campfire stays unlit.
guide.forever.fire_starting.failure: If lighting fails, check that you used the ignition tool directly on the campfire block and that the campfire is placed rather than held.
guide.forever.fire_starting.ignite: Use the ignition tool on the placed campfire to light it.
guide.forever.fire_starting.inputs: You need logs and sticks for the campfire itself, and flint for the tool that lights it.
guide.forever.fire_starting.place_target: Place the unlit campfire where you want it. It gives no light or heat until it is lit.
guide.forever.fire_starting.summary: Fire is the first process you need. Everything early, from cooking to smelting, begins here.
guide.forever.fire_starting.title: Starting a Fire
guide.forever.mason_career.careers: A villager with a workplace can take up a career, such as a Mason, and keeps it along with their home and workplace.
guide.forever.mason_career.coin_purse: A Coin Purse holds your currency as a balance, so money does not fill your inventory.
guide.forever.mason_career.knowledge_aft: If a professional dies, everything they taught survives in the people they taught it to. Knowledge they never passed on is lost with them.
guide.forever.mason_career.mentors_appre: A skilled villager can teach an apprentice. Teaching is how a settlement keeps knowledge rather than holding it in one person.
guide.forever.mason_career.obols: Obols also exist as real items. You can withdraw coins from your purse to carry, trade, or display, and deposit them again later.
guide.forever.mason_career.ranks: Careers advance through ranks: Apprentice, Journeyman, then Master. Rank reflects demonstrated technique and knowledge, not time served.
guide.forever.mason_career.summary: Villagers build real careers, and Obols are the currency they trade in.
guide.forever.mason_career.title: Village Careers and Obols
guide.forever.mastery_loadout.focus_and_: You may run one Focus mastery and up to two Supporting masteries at a time.
guide.forever.mastery_loadout.permanent_: Everything you have learned is permanent. Masteries you set aside keep all of their progress, and you never lose experience, levels, or coins by changing your loadout.
guide.forever.mastery_loadout.summary: Masteries are the specialties you develop. You choose which ones are active without giving up the others.
guide.forever.mastery_loadout.switching: Change your loadout while resting at a home or workplace. Switching is free.
guide.forever.mastery_loadout.title: Masteries and Your Loadout
guide.forever.mastery_loadout.where_to_s: You cannot change your loadout in the middle of a journey. Return to a home or workplace to rest and rearrange.
guide.forever.mastery_progression.breadt: Breadth counts. Working with materials, places, and situations you have not handled before advances a mastery further than repeating familiar work.
guide.forever.mastery_progression.discov: First-time discoveries count. Finding a new ore, reaching a new depth, or reaching a new region are all recorded once.
guide.forever.mastery_progression.not_re: Mining the same block ten thousand times will not advance a mastery. Repetition is not mastery here, so there is nothing to gain from grinding one action.
guide.forever.mastery_progression.projec: Completed projects count. Finishing substantial work advances mastery more than any single action.
guide.forever.mastery_progression.summar: Mastery grows through what you accomplish, not through how many times you repeat one action.
guide.forever.mastery_progression.techni: Technique counts. Doing difficult work well is recognised.
guide.forever.mastery_progression.title: How Mastery Advances
guide.forever.settlement_charter.charter: A Settlement Charter founds a settlement. Nothing becomes a settlement by accident.
guide.forever.settlement_charter.graph_a: New buildings join a settlement by being near one that is already registered. Distant production sites can be registered as outposts and linked later.
guide.forever.settlement_charter.no_styl: Build in any style you like. Settlements are never scored on appearance, and there is no required theme or blueprint.
guide.forever.settlement_charter.registe: You register a building yourself by marking its bounds. The game never scans your world looking for structures, so a build only counts once you say it counts.
guide.forever.settlement_charter.residen: A residence is checked for function: enclosure, a bed, storage, safety, and enough space. If a check fails, you are told exactly which requirement is unmet.
guide.forever.settlement_charter.summary: A settlement is a group of buildings you have registered. It grows as you add more.
guide.forever.settlement_charter.title: Founding and Growing a Settlement
guide.forever.storage_travelers_cache.ca: A Traveler's Cache starts with nine slots.
guide.forever.storage_travelers_cache.ex: It can later be expanded to eighteen slots.
guide.forever.storage_travelers_cache.no: Containers cannot be placed inside a Traveler's Cache. Shulker boxes, backpacks, crates, and similar storage items are refused, so a cache can never become unlimited storage.
guide.forever.storage_travelers_cache.ph: The index only reports what is really in your containers. If the two ever disagree, the actual contents win. Items are never pulled to you from across the world.
guide.forever.storage_travelers_cache.se: You can search the index for an item and learn where it is stored.
guide.forever.storage_travelers_cache.su: The Traveler's Cache carries personal essentials. Warehouses handle bulk at home.
guide.forever.storage_travelers_cache.wa: A warehouse indexes containers you have registered, letting you see what your settlement holds.
